title: Rigveda 4.9: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.9: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.9 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 265r-265v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.9.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 5, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 265r
translation.original_text:
1agne̍ mṛ̱ḻa ma̱hām̐ a̍si̱ ya ī̱m ā de̍va̱yuṁ jana̍m | i̱yetha̍ ba̱rhir ā̱sada̍m ||
2sa mānu̍ṣīṣu dū̱ḻabho̍ vi̱kṣu prā̱vīr ama̍rtyaḥ | dū̱to viśve̍ṣām bhuvat ||
3sa sadma̱ pari̍ ṇīyate̱ hotā̍ ma̱ndro divi̍ṣṭiṣu | u̱ta potā̱ ni ṣī̍dati ||
4u̱ta gnā a̱gnir a̍dhva̱ra u̱to gṛ̱hapa̍ti̱r dame̍ | u̱ta bra̱hmā ni ṣī̍dati ||
translation.text:
1AGNI, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come, To seat thee on the sacred grass.
2May he the Immortal, Helper, hard to be deceived among mankind, Become the messenger of all.
3Around the altar is he led, welcome Chief Priest at solemn rites, Or as the Potar sits him down.
4Agni in fire at sacrifice, and in the house as Lord thereof, And as a Brahman takes his seat.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 265r (numbered 74r by the scribe) (OPenn image 265, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.8.5 ‹-puṣyantaḥ indhate›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 265v (numbered 74v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.9.5 ‹-janānām havyā ca mānuṣāṇām›. Verses 4.9.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1agne | mṛḷa | mahān | asi | yaḥ | īm | ā | deva-yum | janam | iyetha | barhiḥ | āsadam
2saḥ | mānuṣīṣu | duḥ-dabhaḥ | vikṣu | pra-avīḥ | amartyaḥ | dūtaḥ | viśveṣām | bhuvat
3saḥ | sadma | pari | nīyate | hotā | mandraḥ | diviṣṭiṣu | uta | potā | ni | sīdati
4uta | gnāḥ | agniḥ | adhvare | uto iti | gṛha-patiḥ | dame | uta | brahmā | ni | sīdati

translation.original_ref: RV 4.9.5-8 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 5, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 265v
translation.original_text:
5veṣi̱ hy a̍dhvarīya̱tām u̍pava̱ktā janā̍nām | ha̱vyā ca̱ mānu̍ṣāṇām ||
6veṣīd v a̍sya dū̱tya1̱̍ṁ yasya̱ jujo̍ṣo adhva̱ram | ha̱vyam marta̍sya̱ voḻha̍ve ||
7a̱smāka̍ṁ joṣy adhva̱ram a̱smāka̍ṁ ya̱jñam a̍ṅgiraḥ | a̱smāka̍ṁ śṛṇudhī̱ hava̍m ||
8pari̍ te dū̱ḻabho̱ ratho̱ 'smām̐ a̍śnotu vi̱śvata̍ḥ | yena̱ rakṣa̍si dā̱śuṣa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
5Thou comest as the guide of folk who celebrate a sacrifice, And to oblations brought by men.
6Thou servest as his messenger whose sacrifice thou lovest well, To bear the mortal's gifts to heaven.
7Accept our solemn rite; be pleased, Angiras, with our sacrifice: Give ear and listen to our call.
8May thine inviolable car, wherewith thou guardest those who give, Come near to us from every side.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 265v (numbered 74v by the scribe) (OPenn image 266, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.9.5 ‹-janānām havyā ca mānuṣāṇām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 266r (numbered 75r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.10.4 ‹divaḥ na stanayanti śuṣmāḥ›. Verses 4.9.5-8 end on this page; 4.9.5 begins on fol. 265r (numbered 74r by the scribe).

6veṣi | it | oṃ iti | asya | dūtyam | yasya | jujoṣaḥ | adhvaram | havyam | martasya | voḷhave
7asmākam | joṣi | adhvaram | asmākam | yajñam | aṅgiraḥ | asmākam | śṛṇudhi | havam
